name: Budae Jjigae (Korean Army Base Stew)
why: Korea's great post-war street-food invention — a bubbling pot of gochujang, kimchi and Spam that's now a national obsession. Hands-off, feeds a crowd, and the next chapter in your Korean cuisine experiments.
ingredients: 2 instant ramen cakes (Sari gomtang beef bone soup flavour is best)
1 spring onion, cut into 3-4 cm lengths
1.5 tbsp Korean soup soy sauce or light soy sauce
2 tbsp gochugaru (fine Korean red pepper flakes)

steps: Combine the gochujang, doenjang, garlic, soup soy sauce, gochugaru, black pepper and sugar in a bowl and let it sit for 5 minutes so the flavours meld.
Dissolve the ramen flavour sachet(s) into the 500 ml hot water.
Arrange all the base ingredients — kimchi, Spam, onion, spring onion, baked beans, cheese slice, frankfurts and tteok — in a large heavy-based saucepan or wide pot.
Pour the seasoned water and the chilli paste into the pot over the arranged ingredients — don't stir, let each section keep its place.
Bring to a rolling boil over medium-high heat, then add the instant ramen cakes to the broth.
Boil for 5-8 minutes until the noodles have softened and absorbed the broth.
Remove from the heat and top with an extra slice of processed cheese to melt over the noodles.
Sprinkle generously with toasted sesame seeds and serve straight from the pot with steamed rice on the side.

pro_tips: For a milder pot, use Soon Chang brand gochujang — it's noticeably less hot than the standard red-label jars.

Arrange the ingredients in neat sections rather than stirring them in — the whole joy of budae jjigae is diving into your favourite part of the pot. Add a splash more of the seasoned broth if it reduces too far.
author: Henry
